requirements.condition: For destinations listed in an UPDATE message
requirements.required_behavior: The router identified by the IP address in NEXT_HOP SHOULD be used as the next hop.
requirements.why_checkable: NEXT_HOP interpretation can be checked against the UPDATE destinations and routing decision.

         interface that is used to reach the peer).
requirements.condition: When announcing a locally originated route to an internal peer, subject to the directly connected and peer-address exceptions
requirements.required_behavior: The speaker SHOULD use the interface address of the router through which the announced network is reachable as NEXT_HOP.
requirements.why_checkable: Locally originated route advertisements expose the selected next-hop address.

requirements.condition: When announcing a locally originated route to an internal peer and the route is directly connected, or its reachable router interface address is the internal peer address
requirements.required_behavior: The speaker SHOULD use its own IP address of the interface used to reach the peer as NEXT_HOP.
requirements.why_checkable: Both exception cases can be matched against advertised NEXT_HOP and the local peer-facing interface.

requirements.quote:
2) When sending a message to an external peer, X, and the peer is
         one IP hop away from the speaker:

         - If the route being announced was learned from an internal
           peer or is locally originated, the BGP speaker can use an
           interface address of the internal peer router (or the
           internal router) through which the announced network is
           reachable for the speaker for the NEXT_HOP attribute,
           provided that peer X shares a common subnet with this
           address.  This is a form of "third party" NEXT_HOP attribute.
requirements.condition: When advertising to an external peer X one IP hop away, and the route was learned internally or originated locally
requirements.required_behavior: The speaker can use the interface address of the internal peer router or internal router through which the network is reachable as a third-party NEXT_HOP, provided X shares a common subnet with that address.
requirements.why_checkable: The allowed third-party address can be checked against route origin, reachability, and peer subnet membership.

requirements.quote:
- Otherwise, if the route being announced was learned from an
           external peer, the speaker can use an IP address of any
           adjacent router (known from the received NEXT_HOP attribute)
           that the speaker itself uses for local route calculation in
           the NEXT_HOP attribute, provided that peer X shares a common
           subnet with this address.  This is a second form of "third
           party" NEXT_HOP attribute.
requirements.condition: When advertising to an external peer X one IP hop away, otherwise if the route was learned from an external peer
requirements.required_behavior: The speaker can use the IP address of an adjacent router known from the received NEXT_HOP and used for local route calculation as third-party NEXT_HOP, provided X shares a common subnet with that address.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected address can be compared with learned NEXT_HOP, local route calculation, and X subnet membership.

requirements.quote:
- Otherwise, if the external peer to which the route is being
           advertised shares a common subnet with one of the interfaces
           of the announcing BGP speaker, the speaker MAY use the IP
           address associated with such an interface in the NEXT_HOP
           attribute.  This is known as a "first party" NEXT_HOP
           attribute.
requirements.condition: When advertising to a one-hop external peer, otherwise if that peer shares a subnet with a speaker interface
requirements.required_behavior: The speaker MAY use the IP address associated with that interface as first-party NEXT_HOP.
requirements.why_checkable: An optional first-party address choice is verifiable against the interface and shared subnet.

requirements.quote:
- By default (if none of the above conditions apply), the BGP
           speaker SHOULD use the IP address of the interface that the
           speaker uses to establish the BGP connection to peer X in the
           NEXT_HOP attribute.
requirements.condition: When advertising to external peer X one IP hop away and none of the preceding address-selection conditions applies
requirements.required_behavior: By default, the speaker SHOULD use the IP address of the interface used to establish the BGP connection to X as NEXT_HOP.
requirements.why_checkable: The default advertisement can be compared with the BGP connection interface address.

requirements.quote:

           speaker learned from one of its peers, the NEXT_HOP attribute
           of the advertised route is exactly the same as the NEXT_HOP
requirements.condition: When sending to an external peer multiple IP hops away
requirements.required_behavior: The speaker MAY be configured to propagate NEXT_HOP.
requirements.why_checkable: Configuration and advertisement behavior can reveal whether this optional mode is provided.

requirements.quote:
- The speaker MAY be configured to propagate the NEXT_HOP
           attribute.  In this case, when advertising a route that the
           speaker learned from one of its peers, the NEXT_HOP attribute
           of the advertised route is exactly the same as the NEXT_HOP

           attribute of the learned route (the speaker does not modify
           the NEXT_HOP attribute).
requirements.condition: When configured to propagate NEXT_HOP to a multihop external peer and advertising a route learned from a peer
requirements.required_behavior: Advertise exactly the NEXT_HOP attribute of the learned route.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Modify the learned NEXT_HOP attribute in this propagation mode.
requirements.why_checkable: Received and advertised NEXT_HOP values can be compared under the propagation setting.

requirements.quote:
- By default, the BGP speaker SHOULD use the IP address of the
           interface that the speaker uses in the NEXT_HOP attribute to
           establish the BGP connection to peer X.
requirements.condition: When sending to an external peer X multiple IP hops away, under default behavior
requirements.required_behavior: The speaker SHOULD use the IP address of the interface used to establish the BGP connection to X as NEXT_HOP.
requirements.why_checkable: The default multihop advertisement can be matched to its connection interface.

requirements.quote:
Normally, the NEXT_HOP attribute is chosen such that the shortest
   available path will be taken.  A BGP speaker MUST be able to support
   the disabling advertisement of third party NEXT_HOP attributes in
   order to handle imperfectly bridged media.
requirements.condition: For BGP speakers
requirements.required_behavior: The speaker MUST support disabling advertisement of third-party NEXT_HOP attributes.
requirements.why_checkable: A configuration mechanism and its effect on third-party advertisements can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
A route originated by a BGP speaker SHALL NOT be advertised to a peer
   using an address of that peer as NEXT_HOP.  A BGP speaker SHALL NOT
   install a route with itself as the next hop.
requirements.condition: When advertising a route originated by this BGP speaker to a peer
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The speaker SHALL NOT advertise the route using an address of that peer as NEXT_HOP.
requirements.why_checkable: An originated route advertised to a peer can be checked for a peer-owned NEXT_HOP address.

requirements.quote:
A route originated by a BGP speaker SHALL NOT be advertised to a peer
   using an address of that peer as NEXT_HOP.  A BGP speaker SHALL NOT
   install a route with itself as the next hop.
requirements.condition: When installing a route
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The speaker SHALL NOT install a route with itself as the next hop.
requirements.why_checkable: Route installation can be checked for rejection of self-referential next hops.

requirements.quote:
The NEXT_HOP attribute is used by the BGP speaker to determine the
   actual outbound interface and immediate next-hop address that SHOULD
   be used to forward transit packets to the associated destinations.
requirements.condition: When forwarding transit packets to destinations associated with NEXT_HOP
requirements.required_behavior: Use NEXT_HOP to determine the actual outbound interface, which SHOULD be used to forward those packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Forwarding interface selection can be traced to resolution of the advertised NEXT_HOP.

requirements.quote:

requirements.condition: When forwarding transit packets to destinations associated with NEXT_HOP
requirements.required_behavior: Use NEXT_HOP to determine the immediate next-hop address, which SHOULD be used to forward those packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Forwarding next-hop selection can be traced to the advertised NEXT_HOP.

requirements.quote:
The immediate next-hop address is determined by performing a
   recursive route lookup operation for the IP address in the NEXT_HOP
   attribute, using the contents of the Routing Table, selecting one
   entry if multiple entries of equal cost exist.  The Routing Table
   entry that resolves the IP address in the NEXT_HOP attribute will
   always specify the outbound interface.  If the entry specifies an
   attached subnet, but does not specify a next-hop address, then the
   address in the NEXT_HOP attribute SHOULD be used as the immediate
   next-hop address.  If the entry also specifies the next-hop address,
   this address SHOULD be used as the immediate next-hop address for
   packet forwarding.
requirements.condition: When determining the immediate next-hop address
requirements.required_behavior: Perform recursive route lookup for the IP address in NEXT_HOP using the Routing Table.
requirements.why_checkable: Recursive next-hop resolution can be observed with a route whose NEXT_HOP needs another route lookup.
